newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel unveils securities reform proposals.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel unveils securities reform proposals.

text.p: A special committee of an advisory panel to the finance minister unveiled 22 items on Friday which it may propose to make Japan's securities markets more attractive.

The committee, set up in June to debate structural reforms in Japan's securities markets, will help realise Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's plan for a Japanese version of the "Big Bang", said Shoichi Royama, who heads the special committee.
Hashimoto earlier this month revealed plans to liberalise financial markets and to catch up with reforms carried out more than a decade ago in Europe and the United States.
Royama told reporters major changes in Japanese financial and capital markets must take place for that to happen.
It is also increasingly important for funds to be allocated to newly established industries, he said.
"The securities market must take a major role in allocating funds to new industries... It is difficult to do so under the traditional (funding) system centred on bank loans," he said.
He said the committee will finalise its proposals next June after discussing the 22 items.
They include deregulation of brokers' commissions and the diversification the business brokers can conduct.
The proposals would also look at ways to improve ways to assess brokers' financial health and establish a system to cope with brokerage failures.
They would allow new firms to enter the securities field, and allow the offering of a variety of securities products, such as derivatives.
He said the proposals would seek to cut the cost of securities transactions by looking into the securities transaction tax.
The proposals also include allowing holding companies in Japan.
They call for a review of the current system of concentrating securities transactions on stock exchanges, including looking at securities transactions through the Internet.
They would also ease restrictions on listing and publicly offering shares.
